caveat: ANALYTIC ILLUSTRATION, not a measurement of the norm_grpo/norm_dr_grpo runs. The fixed K-cache was generated by a different policy snapshot; this shows what the two normalizers do to a fixed completion-length distribution, not gradient data from the actual forks (those give held-out reward/KL/length via task3_grpo.evaluate).
advantage_source: local reconstruction (r-mu)/(sigma+eps), additive eps, NOT grpo.py
clipped_inclusion_note: clipped_at_max completions ARE included. Step 1 masks max-length completions from the TRAINING loss; this diagnostic is an analytic illustration of the normalization's length-weighting across the realized length distribution, and the long/clipped tail is exactly where the two normalizers differ most, so excluding it would blunt the contrast.
L_max_note: cancels in every correlation and long/short ratio; only rescales absolute means.
gradient_model: first-order (ratio rho=1) GRPO gradient magnitude placed on response k: per token |A_k|/denom_k, per sequence |A_k|*T_k/denom_k; denom_k=T_k (canonical) or L_max (Dr. GRPO). Exact at the epoch-0 ratio used by our 1-epoch updates.
